_comment: Shared cross-group front door. See Architecture & File System §4C/§5/§6 and Decision Tree JSON Build master §3A-§3C/§6. Router-tier only: clinical_presentation (Stage 0) and site_capture (Stage 1) live here, never in a group_XX_dt.json. Moment 1 narrowing implemented 4 Sep 2026: the presentation gives an advisory candidate list, the discriminator drops what its answer excludes, and the topography intersects what is left. The family question is asked only when more than one group survives all three, and never when none of the survivors is built.

archetypes.label: Blood / marrow signs (cytopenias, blasts)
archetypes.scaffold: straight to marrow morphology + flow/IHC (no mass, no imaging)

archetypes.label: Mass / swelling (solid tumour)
archetypes.notes: A survivor site question resolves most cases (Design Spec §3.4). Abdominal/retroperitoneal mass needs one extra organ-of-origin question and may hand off outside candidate_groups (e.g. bowel/nodal → Group II Burkitt). Limb/trunk lesion of unclear origin asks tumour_origin (bone vs soft tissue) for the Ewing 9260 split.

archetypes.label: Lymphadenopathy
archetypes.notes: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §3.5). In a KSHV-endemic paediatric population the dominant form of Kaposi sarcoma is lymphadenopathic, often with few or no skin lesions (Kamiyango W, et al. Cancer and Metastasis Reviews 2019). A lymph node biopsy diagnosed as Kaposi sarcoma (9140/3, ICCC-3 IXc at any site) must be able to reach Group IX by the presentation path, not only by the alias lane.

archetypes.label: Organ-functional sign (leukocoria, proptosis, haematuria, jaundice + AFP, raised ICP)
Incidental imaging finding
archetypes.notes: candidate_groups was the string "all" until 4 Sep 2026; the engine read it as an empty list and this presentation could not be used at all.

archetypes.label: Not sure / mixed presentation
archetypes.scaffold: skip the archetype scaffold → straight to site capture
archetypes.notes: Ambiguous or blurred presentations (leukaemia/lymphoma overlap, a mass with cytopenias) degrade gracefully to site-first entry rather than a silent wrong guess. candidate_groups was the string "all" until 4 Sep 2026; the engine read it as an empty list and this presentation could not be used at all.

primary_compartment.question: Where is the disease centred?

options.label: An organ or tissue outside nodes and marrow

marrow.because: Marrow-based disease is Group I, not a lymphoma.

nodal.because: Nodal disease is Group II, not a leukaemia.

extranodal.because: Extranodal disease is Group II, not a leukaemia.

primary_compartment.hint: Marrow means the blood and bone marrow are the main site. Nodal means lymph nodes. Extranodal means a solid organ or tissue outside nodes and marrow. This is the split between a leukaemia and a lymphoma.
primary_compartment.authoring_note: Group I vs Group II split for 9811-9819 (B-ALL family), 9823 (SLL/CLL), 9827 (ATLL) when the compartment (not topography alone) determines the group. See dual_group_rules.

tumour_origin.question: Does the tumour arise in bone, or in the soft tissue around it?

options.label: Bone — the lesion is centred in bone, cortex destroyed
Soft tissue — the mass is outside bone, cortex intact

bone.because: Bone origin excludes the extraosseous sarcoma group.

soft_tissue.because: Soft tissue origin excludes the malignant bone tumour group.

tumour_origin.hint: Read it off the imaging. Cortical destruction, periosteal reaction or a lesion centred in the bone means bone. A mass in muscle, fat or connective tissue with the bone intact means soft tissue. If the report does not say, and the mass is not centred on a bone, answer soft tissue.
tumour_origin.authoring_note: Group VIII vs Group IX split for 9364 Ewing sarcoma and 9365 Askin tumour. ICD-O-3.2 deleted 9260/3 and moved Ewing sarcoma to 9364/3. See dual_group_rules.

tree_selection._comment: Site cannot select the tree (every Group I case is C42.x) and blast % may be unknown at entry (Pathway §7.1). This is a second one-tap DATA-LEVEL option appended to Stage 1 site_capture, distinct from organ-of-origin site capture used by solid-tumour archetypes.
tree_selection.question: Dominant marrow pattern (one tap)?
tree_selection.default_rationale: A missed AML/APL is the costlier error, so an unknown or undocumented pattern defaults to the acute-leukaemia tree rather than a lower-acuity tree.

options.label: Chronic myeloid proliferation / high counts, no blasts

tree_selection._comment: Group II's four families diverge before any marker is read, and site cannot separate them: a skin lesion, a lytic bone lesion and a node can all be lymphoid, histiocytic or mast cell (Pathway §7.1). This is a second one-tap DATA-LEVEL option appended to Stage 1, the same mechanism Group 1 uses for dominant_marrow_pattern — not organ-of-origin site capture. Cutaneous and mast-cell presentations must not be forced down the nodal flow.
tree_selection.question: What does the lesion look like on the report (one tap)?
tree_selection.default_rationale: A lymphoid mass is by a wide margin the commonest Group II presentation, and the main tree carries the not-lymphoma gate and the compartment gate that every other tree assumes has already been passed. An unclassified or undocumented presentation therefore defaults here rather than to a narrower tree that would skip those gates.

options.label: Lymphadenopathy or a nodal / extranodal mass
Histiocytic / dendritic proliferation (incl. lytic bone lesion, CD1a or S100 positive)
Mast cell infiltrate (tryptase or CD117 positive, urticaria pigmentosa)

3.name: CNS and Miscellaneous Intracranial and Intraspinal Neoplasms

tree_routing._comment: Group III keys its trees to anatomical COMPARTMENT, not to histological family: CNS5 defines ependymoma by compartment, ICCC-3 splits 9380 and gates 8158/8290/9501-9504/8000-8005 by topography, and the paediatric posterior fossa differential is a compartment differential before it is a histological one (Pathway Revision 2 §6.3). The compartment is already known from the Stage 1 topography, so NO extra question is asked of the clerk — unlike Group 2, whose four families diverge before any marker is read and which therefore needs tree_selection. The map below is total and disjoint over all 25 topography codes the group can carry; build_database.py rule 12 sweeps it.

rules.label: Midline — sellar, suprasellar, pineal, optic pathway, cranial nerve
Site not established, overlapping, or nervous system NOS

default.label: Site not established
default.reason: A Group III case whose topography resolves to no compartment cannot be routed on site. g3_unspecified carries the IIIf five-point flag and the ENCR basis-of-diagnosis computation, which is exactly what such a case needs.

4.name: Neuroblastoma and Other Peripheral Nervous Cell Tumours

tree_routing._comment: Group IV's three tumour families separate cleanly on topography, already captured at Stage 1, so the clerk is asked nothing extra -- the same mechanism as Group III's tree_routing (Group 4 build contract §5). The one real overlap, neuroblastoma vs pheochromocytoma at the adrenal, is resolved inside g4_sympathoadrenal by age and catecholamine profile, not here. The map below is total and disjoint over every topography code topography_codes.json currently associates with Group 4 (candidate_groups including 4, plus C48.2 and C80.9 -- see build report), with g4_other_peripheral as the catch-all. NOT yet routable: the build contract's own §5 architecture table names C10.x (oropharynx), C32.x (larynx) and C77.0 (lymph nodes of head/face/neck) as g4_head_neck_paraganglia topography, but none of the three exists in topography_codes.json yet, so none is included below -- reported, not invented.

rules.label: Sympathoadrenal -- adrenal medulla/cortex, peripheral nerve and autonomic nervous system, retroperitoneum/peritoneum, mediastinum
Head and neck paraganglia -- carotid body, aortic body/other paraganglia (incl. jugulotympanic), middle ear
Sinonasal -- nasal cavity, accessory sinuses, nasopharynx (olfactory neuroblastoma / sinonasal differential)

default.label: Everything else Group IV can carry
default.reason: A Group IV case whose topography resolves to none of the three site-specific families reaches the catch-all, the analogue of g3_unspecified -- medulloepithelioma/neuroepithelioma at a peripheral site none of the other trees own, an inadequate specimen, or an unestablished site.

9.name: Soft Tissue and Other Extraosseous Sarcomas

tree_routing._comment: Group IX at a skin site (C44) enters g9_skin, the one entry holding Visser 2023 Table 3's basis-1 row for Kaposi sarcoma of the skin; every other topography, and an uncaptured one, enters g9_soft_tissue, where a clinical note cannot register Kaposi sarcoma. Code review, 4 October 2026 (Group 9 build report §13).

default.label: Soft tissue and every other site

11.name: Other Malignant Epithelial Neoplasms and Malignant Melanomas

dual_group_rules._comment: Transcribed from Decision Tree JSON Build master §6. Consulted at Moment 1 (routePresentation, before any tree loads, when candidates.length > 1) and/or Moment 2 (resolveGroup at a terminal, Architecture §6). Engine walks branches[] in order; first match wins; falls to default if none match. | BRANCH `when` VOCABULARY IS CLOSED, and it is closed because it was not. branchMatches() in app.js reads exactly two shapes: `topography_in` (a list) and `captured_variable` with `equals` or with `operator`+`value`. It has never read `topography_equals`, and four branches used it -- 9380 at C72.3, 8158/8290 at C75.1, 8963 at C64.9 and 8000-8005 at C64.9. All four were dead: the branch never matched and every case fell to the rule's default, which for two of them is a different ICCC-3 group. Found and fixed 22 September 2026 during the Group VI build, and check_router_branch_when_vocabulary() now rejects any key branchMatches() does not read.

9811-9819.label: B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma family

branches.note: ≥25% marrow blasts overrides a nodal/extranodal presentation — routes to Group I regardless of compartment.

9811-9819.note: Includes 9819 (B-ALL, BCR::ABL1-like/Ph-like) alongside 9811-9818: 9819 is an ICD-O-3.2 addition postdating DT master §6's table (Pathway §5.7), belongs to the same B-ALL family, and group_01_dt.json sets topography_dependent:true on it with the identical routing note applied to 9811-9818.
9811-9819.spleen_carveout_note: C42.2 (spleen) is deliberately excluded from the C42.x branch here, consistent with the 9591 rule's carve-out -- not a transcription slip. DT master §6's literal text says only 'C42.x' without naming spleen, but the registry reads it the same way it reads 9591 (spleen presentation of a B-ALL-family code is not marrow-primary).

9823.label: B-CLL / small lymphocytic lymphoma
9823.spleen_carveout_note: C42.2 (spleen) is deliberately excluded from the C42.x branch here, consistent with the 9591 rule's carve-out -- not a transcription slip. DT master §6's literal text says only 'C42.x' without naming spleen, but the registry reads it the same way it reads 9591.

9827.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL)
9827.note: HTLV-1 serology mandatory before coding either way (clinical_alert, DT master §5).

9591.label: Malignant lymphoma, non-Hodgkin, NOS
9591.note: Group-1-specific dual-group rule (Pathway §1, §5.3). C42.2 (spleen) and every other site fall to the default — this is exactly why C42.0-C42.4 must be individually addressable in topography_codes.json, not lumped as C42.x.

9501-9504.label: Medulloepithelioma
9501-9504.cns_topography_scope_note: Extended 2026-09-18 to the full C70.0-C72.9 CNS range (all 21 codes topography_codes.json's brain_cns crosswalk enumerates), now that Group III was authored 2026-09-16. Previously covered only the NOS-level codes C70.9/C71.9/C72.9, so a medulloepithelioma at a specific CNS subsite (e.g. C71.6) fell through to the default and misrouted to Group 4. ICCC-3 gives 9501-9504 to Group III (IIIc3) across the whole of C70.0-C72.9, Group 4 only outside it. Group 4 build contract §2.5.

branches.note: At the liver (C22.0, C22.1) an ACTH-producing tumour is ICCC-3 Group VII, subgroup VIIb, hepatic carcinomas.
branches.authoring_note: ICCC-2017 range 70 lists 8158 among the C22 carcinomas at sites 220,221, behaviour 3, subgroup VIIb, and group_07_dt.json carries 8158/3 'ACTH-producing tumor' as a VIIb entry. 8158 shared a rule with 8290 until 4 October 2026; the two no longer route alike, because ICCC-2017 gives 8290 no Group VII row and its XIf10 site list excludes 220-238, so 8158 was split into this rule. Without the branch a hepatic ACTH-producing tumour took the shared rule's group 11 default and never reached Group VII -- the same defect the Group VII build corrected for 8170 (Group 7 build contract Sec.0.2 point 3, Sec.7.1).

9364.label: Ewing sarcoma

default.note: No safe topography default — tumour_origin must be captured; site alone (limb/trunk) does not resolve bone vs soft tissue.

9364.authoring_note: Re-keyed from the former '9260' rule during the Group VIII build, 2 October 2026 (docs/TODO.md §8.1; Group 8 build contract §7). ICD-O-3.2 deleted 9260/3 Ewing sarcoma and moved it to 9364/3 (IARC 'Deleted codes and their terms', 9 Oct 2020, p. 6); 9260 now carries only 9260/0 Aneurysmal bone cyst, so the old rule matched a code no group emits. Subgroups per ICCC-2017.sqlite: 9364 -> VIIIc2 (range 65, 400-419) / IXd2 (range 81); 9365 -> VIIIc1 (range 64, 400-419) / IXd1 (range 80). Group VIII owns this rule by agreement with the Group IX session.

9365.label: Askin tumour

default.note: No safe topography default — tumour_origin must be captured; site alone (limb/trunk) does not resolve bone vs soft tissue.

9365.authoring_note: Re-keyed from the former '9260' rule during the Group VIII build, 2 October 2026 (docs/TODO.md §8.1; Group 8 build contract §7). ICD-O-3.2 deleted 9260/3 Ewing sarcoma and moved it to 9364/3 (IARC 'Deleted codes and their terms', 9 Oct 2020, p. 6); 9260 now carries only 9260/0 Aneurysmal bone cyst, so the old rule matched a code no group emits. Subgroups per ICCC-2017.sqlite: 9364 -> VIIIc2 (range 65, 400-419) / IXd2 (range 81); 9365 -> VIIIc1 (range 64, 400-419) / IXd1 (range 80). Group VIII owns this rule by agreement with the Group IX session.

8963.label: Rhabdoid tumour, NOS

branches.note: At the liver (C22.0, C22.1) a rhabdoid tumour is ICCC-3 Group VII, subgroup VIIa2, rhabdoid hepatic tumour.
branches.authoring_note: ICCC-2017 range 68: 8963 at sites 220,221, behaviour 3, is VIIa2. Without this branch a hepatic rhabdoid tumour fell to the Group IX IXd3 default, whose site list (000-218,239-639,659-699,739-768,809) excludes 220-238. Added by the Group VII build, 2 October 2026 (Group 7 build contract Sec.7.1).

8963.cns_topography_extended_note: Extended from the three NOS-level codes C70.9/C71.9/C72.9 to all 21 codes in C70.0-C72.9 during the Group VI build, 22 September 2026. The note this replaces said to extend it "when Group III is authored"; Group III was authored on 16 September 2026 and topography_codes.json now enumerates every CNS subsite, so the note's premise was false on its face (docs/TODO.md Sec.12, Group 6 build contract Sec.7.2b). Before this, a case at a SPECIFIC CNS subsite -- C71.6 cerebellum, say -- missed the branch and fell to the default, which ICCC-2017 does not admit at a CNS site at all. For 8963 the default is Group IX IXd3, whose ICCC-2017 site list (000-218,239-639,659-699,739-768,809) excludes 700-729 entirely, so a rhabdoid tumour at a specific CNS subsite named a group ICCC-2017 does not admit there and never reached 9508/3 Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumour.

8991.label: Embryonal sarcoma

branches.note: At the liver (C22.0, C22.1) an embryonal sarcoma is ICCC-3 Group VII, subgroup VIIa3, embryonal sarcoma of liver.
branches.authoring_note: ICCC-2017 range 69: 8991 at sites 220,221, behaviour 3, is VIIa3 (Group 7 build contract Sec.0.2 point 2, Sec.7.1).

8991.default_note: ICCC-2017 range 91 places 8991 in IXa, rhabdomyosarcomas, at sites 000-218,239-809 -- every site except the liver. Rule added by the Group VII build, 2 October 2026; ownership agreed with the Group IX session the same day.

8170.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
8170.default_corrected_note: Default changed from group 11 to group 7 VIIb during the Group VII build, 2 October 2026. ICCC-2017 range 71 places 8160-8162 and 8170-8180 in VIIb at sites 000-809, any site, and no Group XI range carries 8170 at all, so the group 11 default had no basis in the recode (Group 7 build contract Sec.0.2 point 3, Sec.7.1).

8000-8005.label: Malignant neoplasm, NOS (unspecified)

branches.note: ICCC-2017 range 52: 8000-8005 at site 649, behaviour 3, is subgroup VIc, Unspecified malignant renal tumors. Without this branch a malignant renal neoplasm with no pathology fell to the Group XII default and could not reach Group VI at all -- the same defect as a neuroblastoma at C48.2 never reaching Group IV (commit 10ca4fa). Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 5: anything outside Tables 3 and 4 diagnosed without pathology is 8000/3, so this is the modal destination for a renal mass that fails the nephroblastoma imaging constellation (Group 6 build contract Sec.0.11, Sec.3.4).

branches.authoring_note: ICCC-2017 range 71: 8000-8005 at sites 400-419, behaviour 3, is subgroup VIIIe, Unspecified malignant bone tumors; XIIb (range 143) excludes 400-419. The branch records the ICCC-3 fact; it changes nothing on screen, because app.js reads resolveGroup() only for `note` and this branch has none, and nothing reads the routed group (the bone tree's own 8000 entry already carries VIIIe). Added in the Group VIII build, 2 October 2026; Group VII appends a disjoint C22 branch.

branches.note: At the liver (C22.0, C22.1) a malignant neoplasm with no specific type is ICCC-3 Group VII, subgroup VIIc, unspecified malignant hepatic tumours.
branches.authoring_note: ICCC-2017 range 72: 8000-8005 at sites 220,221, behaviour 3, is VIIc. Without this branch a liver case coded 8000/3 fell to the Group XII default, whose XIIb site list excludes 220-238. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 5 (Group 7 build contract Sec.0.6, Sec.7.1).

8000-8005.cns_topography_extended_note: Extended from the three NOS-level codes C70.9/C71.9/C72.9 to all 21 codes in C70.0-C72.9 during the Group VI build, 22 September 2026. The note this replaces said to extend it "when Group III is authored"; Group III was authored on 16 September 2026 and topography_codes.json now enumerates every CNS subsite, so the note's premise was false on its face (docs/TODO.md Sec.12, Group 6 build contract Sec.7.2b). Before this, a case at a SPECIFIC CNS subsite -- C71.6 cerebellum, say -- missed the branch and fell to the default, which ICCC-2017 does not admit at a CNS site at all. For 8000-8005 the default is Group XII, whose XIIb site list excludes 700-729 and 751-753. C75.1, C75.2 and C75.3 were already present and are kept -- they match ICCC-2017 range 42's 700-729,751-753.

9930.label: Myeloid sarcoma
9930.note: Always Group I (Ib), regardless of presenting site. An orbital, cutaneous, nodal or other extramedullary myeloid sarcoma must NOT be re-routed to Group II or IX. Record the involved site in topography — it does not change the group.

tick_vocabularies._comment: Closed lists a tick_list node may point to by name (spec 2026-10-06-ux-overall-fixes-design.md section 4). The engine knows no item by name; it reads them here. `variable` is the case variable the ticked ids are kept in, an array in list order.

evidence_documents.label: Documents in file
evidence_documents.prompt: Tick every report that is in the file.
evidence_documents.none_label: None of these. Code from the reports ticked above.
